phenomenon_scale.label: 112 µm
phenomenon_scale.observable: Turing spot wavelength of trichome initiation on the leaf-primordium epidermis

paleobiology.note: Single extant point. No fossil chronospecies predecessor is in this series. The comparison is the scale ladder at 0 Ma.

predecessor.name: pavement cell
predecessor.state: subcritical homogeneous epidermis; one cell cannot fit λ_c

successor.name: young leaf
successor.state: same λ_c; domain growth inserts more trichomes

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + Du lap u; dv/dt = b - u^2 v + Dv lap v
equations.mapping: u = GL1/GL3/TTG1 activator complex; v = mobile TTG1 substrate (Bouyer trapping/depletion)
equations.turing_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv); lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c
equations.source: Turing 1952, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72, doi:10.1098/rstb.1952.0012

empirical_claims.claim: TTG1 protein moves between cells, accumulates in incipient trichomes, and is depleted around them in a GL3-dependent trapping mechanism that can pattern a 2D epidermis.
The trichome core network combines activator-inhibitor (long-range CPC) and activator-depletion (short-range TRY) paths; weak ttg1 alleles constrain that model space.
Wild-type Arabidopsis trichome patterns have fat-tailed power spectra, read as noise-driven stochastic Turing patterns rather than a purely deterministic instability.

boundary_conditions: Periodic square patch, side equal to four critical wavelengths (446.4 µm), representing a primordium-detail window rather than a whole leaf.
